brief: A compact desk unit with a drawer, plus a spike at a corner where three bases meet to hold a small platform.

requirements.evidence: Three full hex bases at (0,0), (1,0) and (0,1) form a compact triangular cluster; the open faces are closed with 10 solid caps and the joints are locked with bolts. check_build is ok with meshClash clear.

A drawer frame notch (notch:0#-1,1, stem hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf) sits in the empty cell at (-1,1) beside the bases at (0,0) and (0,1). No separate drawer-front or insert was added, so the drawer is the frame notch only.

requirements.requirement: Spike at a corner where three bases meet
requirements.evidence: A mount-type spike (spike:0#0,0|0,1|1,0) sits at the junction where bases (0,0), (1,0) and (0,1) meet.
setSpikeAccessory platform-sm is applied to that spike, so the small platform (platform-sm) is carried on it. The stud-type spike refused a platform, so the mount type was used.

finish.summary: Built a compact desk unit: three full hex bases in a triangle, a drawer frame notch beside two of them, and a mount spike at the three-base corner carrying a small platform. Caps and joint bolts close and lock the cluster; check_build reports no issues and a clear mesh. I added no props, since the brief concerns structure rather than use.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
